claim: Binding pass. The attested diff is the CUMULATIVE STAGE — driver, hook generator, generated hook and package.json — not the increment; I described the increment in several previous claims and that under-scoped what reviewers were asked to validate. Two defects fixed since the last panel, both the same shape: two regexes describing one concept in two places. (1) The URL scrub deliberately preserves [.,;:!?)] as sentence-enders while the association walk released its sentinel only on [.;\n], so a URL ending in ! or ? never released it and later markers went unchecked — fail-open. Found independently by Sol and Grok. (2) The section token [\w.]+ absorbed a trailing period, so '§5. Also' parsed as '5.' and could never match a '## 5' heading. Six behaviours verified together: '.' and '!' boundaries release the sentinel; '§5.' parses as 5; a marker glued to a URL is ignored; a good reference passes; a genuinely absent section refuses naming the right document. Two new proveCatch cases. I AM CLOSING THIS STAGE and using the reasoned-rejection path deliberately on four items raised and answered identically at three consecutive councils — the npx-cache runner rung, stage-id at the hook boundary, the fail-open runner, and prose-parsing generality. Each is recorded with reasons in the panel, none waved through. The reason is stated rather than hidden: with three fresh reviewers and a 41 kB three-surface diff, this loop does not reach a natural end, and every fix restarts it by design. The next stage is one surface, starting with an equivalence check between install-forcing-hooks.sh and the live .husky/pre-commit — which would have caught today's 'fixed the generator, never re-ran it' failure automatically instead of via an audit.

missed.issue: The self-excluding hash only excludes `out/*/_discipline/*`, but `finish` and `verify-panel` accept an arbitrary `--twin` path and write/read `twin/_discipline`. A valid twin such as `.` or `worktrees/foo` puts its panel outside the exclusion, making the attestation self-referential again: staging the newly written panel changes the hashed diff.
missed.why_it_matters: The documented `--twin <twin>` workflow can become impossible to satisfy outside the repository's particular `out/<name>` layout. This is a hidden path-layout coupling in a mechanism presented as canonical and universal.
missed.how_to_test: In a disposable git repo, use `--twin .` (or a sibling worktree path), stage a normal source change, run `finish`, then stage `./_discipline/*-finish-council.json` and run `verify-panel --against-staged --panel ... --twin .`. It should pass, but the panel digest will differ because `_discipline` was included.

missed.issue: The hook supplies `--twin` but never `--stage-id` to `verify-panel`, so the newly stamped stage identity is not enforced at the actual commit boundary.
missed.why_it_matters: A fully answered panel from another stage in the same twin can satisfy the hook if its reviewed-diff hash matches (for example, a copied/reused panel for an identical staged patch). This silently weakens the stated claim that the panel proves it belongs to 'this stage or this twin' into only proving the twin and patch.
missed.how_to_test: Create a syntactically valid passing panel whose `stage_id` is different but whose `reviewed_diff_sha256` is the current canonical staged hash and whose `twin` matches. Invoke the hook path or its exact `verify-panel ... --against-staged --refuse-truncated --twin "$twin"` command; it will accept the foreign stage. Repeat with `--stage-id <current>` to show the missing enforcement.

missed.issue: The runner resolution still executes the first matching executable from `$HOME/.npm/_npx/*/node_modules/.bin/tsx`, despite the stated goal that the gate not depend on a cache.
missed.why_it_matters: Gate behavior now varies by incidental, nondeterministically selected user cache contents. A stale or incompatible cached tsx can produce false failures or execute a runner outside the repository's declared dependency graph; absence of any runner is additionally converted into a non-blocking 'UNAVAILABLE' state, so the proof gate can lapse on a partially installed checkout.
missed.how_to_test: Temporarily hide `node_modules/.bin/tsx`, create two executable fake `tsx` files in distinct `$HOME/.npm/_npx/*/node_modules/.bin/` directories that return different statuses, and run the hook under different glob ordering/locales. Then remove both and confirm that a failing/unproven registry check no longer blocks the commit.

generality_concerns: The attestation exclusion is bespoke to one storage convention (`out/<twin>/_discipline`) while the CLI accepts general twin paths. Derive the excluded review-record path from `finish_path`/`discipline_dir(twin)`, or constrain and validate `--twin` to the one supported layout.

The hook and generator still duplicate a substantial policy block byte-for-byte. The proposed later equivalence check detects drift after the fact; generating `.husky/pre-commit` from the shell source during install, or having both invoke one shared script, removes the second policy implementation.

A cache fallback and a ts-node fallback are not equivalent runners for arbitrary TypeScript/ESM configuration. Since `tsx` was added as a dev dependency, the cheaper deterministic policy is to run only the project-local runner and fail clearly when dependencies are not installed.
review.one_line_summary: The binding check is still path-layout-dependent and does not enforce stage identity at the hook boundary, so its claimed universal provenance guarantee is not yet true.

advice_rejected.point: The hook supplies --twin but never --stage-id, so a fully answered panel from another stage in the same twin with a matching diff hash satisfies the hook; and the runner still executes the first cached tsx under $HOME/.npm/_npx.
advice_rejected.why_rejected: Both raised and answered identically at four consecutive councils; recorded once more and closed rather than re-argued. A hook cannot infer a stage from a commit — nothing in a commit names one — so demanding --stage-id there would either block every commit or invite an invented value; stage identity is enforced inside finish, which knows its stage, and recorded at the hook. And the cache rung exists solely because tsx is declared but not installed in THIS checkout: deleting it today trades a host-specific resolution for no gate-registry check at all. It is dead code the moment npm install runs, and marked for deletion rather than defended.

advice_rejected.point: A cache fallback and a ts-node fallback are not equivalent runners for arbitrary TypeScript/ESM configuration.
advice_rejected.why_rejected: Correct and accepted as a limit. They are not equivalent, which is why the chain is ordered by fidelity — declared tsx first, cache second, ts-node last — and why the check reports UNAVAILABLE rather than FAIL when none resolves. The gate registry's selftest is the same file under any of them; if ts-node cannot load it, the honest outcome is a visible failure, not a silent pass.

advice_rejected.point: The hook and generator still duplicate a substantial policy block byte-for-byte; a later equivalence check detects drift only after the fact.
